in_hebrew.name: לוי
in_hebrew.meaning: בעל השם לוי הוא חטאי משה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: לשם לוי יש משמעות רחבה במסורת היהודית והנוצרית. השם לוי מופיע בספר בראשית בתור אחד מאחיו של יעקב. השם נקשר גם לבנו של יעקב, לוי, שהיה זה שקבע את טעמי הזבחים ואת טקסי הדת. בנוסף, השם לוי נקשר לארבע הבנות של לוי, שהיו נשואות לאנשים שונים, הן בעלות זהות רוחנית והן נשות חיל המצב. בתחום הנוצרי, השם לוי מופיע כאחד השמות הקדושים, ולוי האחד נחשב לאחד הקדושים החשובים ביותר בעולם הנוצרי.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Louis IX is often considered one of the greatest rulers in French history, and his influence extends beyond France as he is also a central character in European and Western history as a whole. His name became popular in Europe due to his reputation for wise, effective governance and piety. He was crowned King of France in 1226, and he led the Seventh Crusade from 1248 to 1254. Beyond his political accomplishments, Louis is remembered for his exceptional character, serving as an example of faith, compassion, and chivalry.
data.spiritual_significance: Louis is a name steeped in Christian spiritual tradition. The saint, Louis IX, is revered for his unwavering faith and piety throughout his reign. He led a devout life, often participating in prayer and fasting, and even reportedly received the stigmata (the wounds of the crucifixion) on his hands, sides, and feet. This spiritual connection continued even during his military campaigns, where he was known to pray before battles and to care for the wounded and sick regardless of their faith. Through his actions and reputation, Saint Louis became an embodiment of faith and charity. Louis as a name represents a deep spiritual connection with God and a commitment to leading a pious life.

historical_references.reference: Louis IV the Fair, called 'Louis the Pious' (814-840 AD), was a Frankish king and the eldest son of Charlemagne. He inherited the Carolingian Empire in 814 AD upon his father's death. His reign was marked by his attempts to establish a fair and just rule, earning him the name 'Louis the Pious'. He was also known for his efforts to reform the Church and ensure the peace and stability of the realm.

Louis XVI (1754-1793), the last Bourbon monarch of France, ruled from 1774 to 1789. He was married to Marie Antoinette and faced significant financial difficulties, which led to the Estates-General being convened in 1789. This event marked the beginning of the French Revolution, resulting in the downfall of the monarchy and the eventual execution of Louis XVI.
